target.title: fix(heartbeat): retry transient EAGAIN/EINTR on session-store and workspace-template reads
target.body:
## Summary

On macOS, heartbeat-driven reads of the session store and workspace bootstrap files can surface transient `EAGAIN`/`EINTR` (`Unknown system error -11`/`-4`) when another process is swapping the file. This is the root cause of the heartbeat failures reported in #99994.

The existing retry loop in `loadSessionStore` was gated to **Windows-only** via `process.platform === "win32" ? 3 : 1`, so macOS and Linux got a single attempt with no retry. The workspace template read in `fileContentDiffersFromTemplate` (`src/agents/workspace.ts`) had **no retry at all** — a single transient `EAGAIN` propagated up and aborted the heartbeat.

## Root cause

`EAGAIN` (errno `-11`) and `EINTR` (errno `-4`) are transient — they surface when the kernel can't immediately satisfy a read against a file being atomically swapped by another writer. The production failure mode on macOS is the `Unknown system error -11` string form, which doesn't always carry a stable `.code` property, so detection has to match on errno and message text too.

## Changes

**`src/config/sessions/store-load.ts`** (Site 1)
- Drop the `win32`-only gate on `maxReadAttempts` → always `3` on every platform.
- The existing `readFileSync` retry loop already catches all errors via a bare `catch`, so this one-line change is the complete fix for this site.
- Comment updated to cite #99994 and explain the macOS/Linux failure mode.

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`** (Site 2)
- Add `isTransientFsError()` classifier handling: `code === EAGAIN | EINTR`, `errno === -11 | -4`, and the macOS `Unknown system error -11` / `system error -4` message forms.
- Wrap `fileContentDiffersFromTemplate` in a 3-attempt retry loop with 50ms between attempts (using the existing `./utils/sleep.js` helper).
- `ENOENT` still returns `false` ("file absent") so callers don't rewrite missing files.
- Non-transient errors propagate.
- Exhausted transient retries return `false` so the caller does **not** rewrite a file we could not read.
- `fileContentDiffersFromTemplate` is exported with an `@internal` JSDoc tag so tests can exercise the retry path directly.

## Tests

**`src/config/sessions/store-load.eagain-retry.test.ts`** (4 cases)
- Persistent `EAGAIN` exhaustion returns an empty store (the existing behavior on Windows, now confirmed on all platforms).

**`src/agents/workspace.eagain-retry.test.ts`** (8 cases × 2 projects = 16 tests)
- `ENOENT` → `false` (file absent).
- Content matches template → `false`.
- Content differs → `true`.
- `EAGAIN` then success → `true` (retry works).
- `EINTR` then success → `true` (retry works).
- Exhausted retries on persistent `EAGAIN` → `false` (no rewrite).
- macOS `Unknown system error -11` message form → retried.
- Non-transient (`EACCES`) → propagated (not swallowed).

## Verification

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` — clean.
- `tsc --noEmit` — clean (no errors on patched files).
- `oxlint` on all 4 changed files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `vitest run` on both new test files — **20/20 passing**.

## Impact

No happy-path change: on a clean read the new code returns immediately. The retry loop only fires on transient errors, and only for 3 attempts with 50ms backoff. This eliminates the heartbeat aborts observed in production on macOS without altering semantics for any non-transient error class.

Closes #99994.
